links.outcome: Inter-rater agreement between two independent annotators establishing ground truth
links.effect: Cohen's kappa 0.83 overall between two independent physicians; lowest for Findings (0.71); disagreements resolved by study coordinators.
links.quote: A high level of IRA with a Cohen’s Kappa of 0.83 was observed between the two researchers performing the manual value assignment.

links.outcome: Overall accuracy, micro/macro metrics with bootstrap confidence intervals and pairwise significance testing
links.effect: Accuracy reported with 95% bootstrap CIs, e.g., 72.9% [69.5–76.4%] for Rombos; Bonferroni-corrected pairwise comparisons; certainty thresholds tested.
links.quote: To assess statistically significant differences, we compared the performance of all five LLMs in a pairwise manner.

links.outcome: Accuracy under different prompt formulations (default, few-shot, CoT, adapted)
links.effect: Default 59.2–72.9%; CoT mixed (Rombos +3.4%, Phi-4 −9.5%); few-shot decreased accuracy for all models; adapted prompts 64.7–85.3%.
links.quote: Few-shot prompting (both 1- and 3-shot prompts) decreased the overall accuracy for all models, with a range of 30.9–67.5% for the 1-shot prompt and 32.3–58.5% for the 3-shot prompt (see Table 2 for detailed results).

links.outcome: Comparison of five candidate open-source LLMs on same data
links.effect: Rombos significantly outperformed other LLMs with default prompt (72.9% vs 59.2–68.5%, p<0.0001) and with adapted prompts (85.3%).
links.quote: The overall accuracy of Rombos was significantly higher compared to each of the other LLMs ( p < 0.0001; see also Supplementary Table 4).

links.outcome: Local performance of LLM extraction against reference standard on local reports
links.effect: Default prompt accuracies 59.2–72.9% on local reports; system failed to consistently give correct answers; no external validation dataset.
links.quote: However, the system failed to consistently give the correct answers.

links.outcome: Accuracy and coverage when restricting to high model certainty classifications
links.effect: Thresholds raised accuracy above 90% for adapted prompts (e.g., Rombos 94.5% at >99.9%) but coverage fell to under 50% (44.0% for Rombos).
links.quote: In the sub-analysis using a threshold for the relative probability (= “certainty” ), an increase in accuracy compared to the baseline was seen across all models and thresholds.

unlisted_practices: Deploying open-source LLMs on local hardware to keep patient data in-house
Using common data elements for standardized extraction structure
Task-specific adapted prompts versus default prompts
Certainty-threshold flagging of low-confidence outputs for human verification

links.effect: Overall Cohen’s Kappa was 0.83 across 1533 CDE values; subgroup kappas ranged 0.71 to 0.95.
links.quote: A high level of IRA with a Cohen’s Kappa of 0.83 was observed between the two researchers performing the manual value assignment.

links.effect: Default prompt accuracies were 72.9%, 61.6%, 59.2%, 64.7%, and 68.5%; Rombos was significantly higher, p < 0.0001.
links.quote: The overall accuracy of Rombos was significantly higher compared to each of the other LLMs ( p < 0.0001; see also Supplementary Table 4).

links.effect: On local reports, adapted-prompt overall accuracies were Rombos 85.3%, solar preview 64.7%, Phi-4 65.0%, Li 77.4%, Lamarck 81.6%.
links.quote: Using the adapted prompts, the system reached overall accuracies of 85.3% [95% CI 82.5–88.0%] for Rombos, of 64.7% [95% CI 62.1–67.7%] for solar preview, of 65.0% [95% CI 62.1–68.0%] for Phi-4, 77.4% [95% CI 74.2–81.1%] for Li, and 81.6% [95% CI 78.9–84.6%] for Lamarck.

links.effect: Certainty thresholds improved accuracy to > 90% but reduced coverage to < 50%.
links.quote: Setting certainty thresholds further improved accuracies to > 90% but reduced the coverage rate to < 50%.

links.effect: Default-prompt LLM accuracies were 59.2-72.9%, implying substantial incorrect classifications.
links.quote: Using default prompts, the LLMs achieved accuracies of 59.2-72.9%.

links.effect: Few-shot prompting decreased all models: 1-shot accuracy 30.9–67.5%; 3-shot accuracy 32.3–58.5%.
links.quote: Few-shot prompting (both 1- and 3-shot prompts) decreased the overall accuracy for all models, with a range of 30.9–67.5% for the 1-shot prompt and 32.3–58.5% for the 3-shot prompt (see Table 2 for detailed results).

Using relative probability thresholds to flag low-certainty classifications for human verification.
